An image is provided at `/app/media/image.jpg`.

You may open, crop or zoom it as needed.

## Question

Focus on the orange and black fish that is partially cut off on the far right side of the image. What direction is it is traveling if it continues on the same path? Is it going up or down and to the left or right?

## What to do

Write your answer to `/app/answer.md`.

**`/app/answer.md` is the only thing that is graded.** Nothing you print to the
terminal, and no other file, is read. If that file is missing or empty when you
stop, the task scores zero however good your analysis was.

You are working against a time limit and will be cut off without warning when it
is reached. So:

1. **Write a complete answer to `/app/answer.md` early** -- as soon as you have a
   defensible answer, before doing any deeper analysis.
2. Then investigate the media further and **overwrite the file** whenever your
   answer improves.

That way the file always holds your best answer so far, and being cut off costs
you refinement rather than the whole attempt. Answer in prose, and state each
point explicitly rather than implying it.

# Which way is the cut-off orange-and-black fish heading?

## Short answer

**It is traveling DOWN and to the LEFT.**

If that fish keeps going on its current path, it will move **downward** (toward the
bottom of the frame) and **leftward** (toward the left side of the frame) — i.e.
diagonally toward the lower-left corner of the picture, at roughly 25–30° below
horizontal. It is heading down-and-left, not up, and not to the right.

## Which fish I mean

The large orange/salmon koi with dark blotches occupying the **bottom-right corner**
of the image. Its body runs off the right-hand edge of the frame, so only part of it
is visible. Its visible portion lies roughly between x ≈ 3400 and the right edge
(x = 4160) of the 4160 × 3120 original, and between y ≈ 2100 and y ≈ 3020.

## How the fish is oriented

The fish's long axis runs diagonally: the body is high on the **right** (running off
the right edge of the frame at about y ≈ 2100–2570) and slopes down to the **left**,
ending in a blunt, rounded dark tip at about (3400, 2650).

That blunt dark tip at the lower-left is the fish's **head**, and the wide body that
runs off the right edge of the frame is its rear half. Since a fish swims in the
direction its head points, the fish is moving down-and-to-the-left. Its tail is
off-frame to the upper right.

## Why the lower-left end is the head, not the tail

I checked this carefully, because the head end is dark and hard to read, and the
answer flips entirely depending on which end is which. Four independent pieces of
evidence all say "head":

1. **It is opaque, like body flesh, not like a fin.** Sampling raw pixels across the
   dark tip (at y = 2644) the blue channel drops from ~175 (open water) to 55–86
   inside the dark mass. That is exactly the same darkness as a transect straight
   across the solid body (blue ≈ 68–86). By contrast, the genuine fin lower down the
   belly (around x = 3830–3900) only dims the blue channel to 118–150 — you can still
   see blue water through it. Fins in this photo are visibly translucent; this tip is
   not. It is solid tissue.

2. **Its edge is hard, like a body outline.** The boundary of the dark tip is a sharp
   step (blue 169 → 146 → 86 over about 20 px), matching the sharpness of the body's
   dorsal outline. The real fin's edge fades gradually over 40+ px and never reaches
   body darkness.

3. **It tapers the wrong way to be a tail.** Measured column by column, the dark tip
   is only ~48 px deep at its leftmost point (x = 3408), ~168 px at x = 3504 and
   ~224 px at x = 3600, merging smoothly into a body that is 280–460 px deep. So it
   is *narrow at the far end and widens toward the body* — the profile of a blunt
   snout deepening into the gill region. A koi's caudal fin does the opposite: narrow
   at the peduncle and flaring out, and it is always at least as deep as the body. A
   125-px-deep rounded lump could not be this fish's tail fin.

4. **Nothing lies beyond it.** Vertical and horizontal pixel transects just outside
   the tip (x = 3355, from y = 2380 to y = 3000; and above/below the tip at x = 3450)
   are clean water at blue ≈ 160–185. There is no faint fin membrane, no upper or
   lower tail lobe, no trailing fan — the fish simply ends there in solid tissue, as
   it would at a snout.

The supporting anatomy fits too: a long dark **pectoral fin** hangs down immediately
behind that head (base around x = 3650–3712, trailing down to y ≈ 3020, almost to the
bottom edge of the photo), and further back along the belly there are two smaller,
translucent fins (pelvic around x = 3824–3940, anal around x = 4060–4145) — the normal
front-to-back fin sequence for a carp/koi whose head is at the lower left.

- **Where it exits:** if it holds that path it swims across and out of the lower-left
